newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas lawmakers urge Clinton to delay air plan.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas lawmakers urge Clinton to delay air plan.

text.p: Arkansas' congressional delegation in a letter this week urged President Clinton to postpone setting strict new air quality standards to avoid a "popular backlash."

"...we urge you to engage in a constructive dialogue with the congressional leadership and proponents and opponents of the proposals to achieve an agreement to postpone the new standards until adequate information is available to the EPA and the public," the lawmakers told their fellow Arkansan.
The Environmental Protection Agency is to decide in July whether to carry out it proposal to set tighter standards against smog and soot.
The proposal, announced in November, has caused an uproar among polluting industries and localities that would be out of compliance with the new federal rule.

"We share a common fear, in light of the sincere disagreements over these proposed standards, that the proposal may attempt to go too far, too quickly," said the letter signed by Democratic Sen. Dale Bumpers, Republican Sen. Tim Hutchinson, and two Republicans and one Democratic representative.
The letter was not signed by Democratic Rep. Vic Snyder, who a spokesman said wanted to learn more about the issue.
The other lawmakers said there were conflicting views on whether the new standards were necessary, and said the public may not be willing to support rules that would be costly to implement.

"It is not in the public interest to engage in a 'showdown' on the proposed (air standards), either in Congress or in the courts. And yet that is exactly the scenario that may unfold if EPA finalizes" the proposal, they said.
